names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 15 iulie, «Sfinții Mucenici Chiric și Iulita», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 15 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Κήρυκος και Ιουλίττα η μητέρα του», with the rank word left off. The page's hymn has the dative «Κηρύκῳ» and its summary verse «υἷα», the son.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 15. јул ст. ст., „Св. муч. Кирик и Јулита.“ — „Св. муч.“ is the rank, which `types` already carries, and the heading enumerates two bare forenames with no by-name, no place and no kinship in them; «son of Julitta» in the display name is the corpus’s own. `foldchk.py` returns no holder and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder, which on a five-letter bare forename is the second piece of luck this range has had and is **the opposite of what the day’s other form got**.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 15 iulie — «Sfinții Mucenici Chiric și Iulita»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Κήρυκος και Ιουλίττα η μητέρα του»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 15 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and pairs mother and son exactly as the Romanian line does. The man is the folder's own: the child of Julitta of Iconium, killed before the governor Alexander at Tarsus. The Greek page adds Iconium as his mother's home, the flight to Seleucia and then to Tarsus, the governor's name, the child's kick and the fall down the steps that broke his skull, and the long list of where his relics are kept — a part of the skull at the monastery of Gregoriou on Athos, part of the right hand at Xenophontos, an incorrupt palm at the Great Meteoron, and more besides. No year is printed; the only mark of time is «έζησε κατά την εποχή του αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού», the reign undated, so nothing is proposed for `dates`. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints one apolytikion, which names both mother and son, and it is taken onto both folders.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.07.2026 (15. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Кирик и Јулита.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, an **enumerated pair both of whose folders this corpus holds and already relates in both directions**, which is the fourth time this range has met that shape. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. The identification is the kinship and the city and the day: the two folders are named for each other, the body gives Iconium of Lycaonia and the flight to Seleucia, and the Romanian and Greek rows stand on this very 15 July. **`dates` WRITTEN WHERE THE FOLDER HAD NONE, AND THE YEAR BELONGS TO BOTH.** `dates: null` before. The Охридски пролог for 15. јул ст. ст. closes the passion „После многих мука и Јулита би мачем посечена, 304. год.“ — after many torments Julitta too was beheaded with the sword, in 304. The year closes the one scene, and „и Јулита“, Julitta too, is what makes it the year of both: the child suffered first and in the same trial, „Видећи како Кирик пострада пре ње“. Neither doxologia nor saint.gr gave a year. So `death` is 304 to 304, display «304», basis traditional, on this folder and on his mother’s. **The age of three is an age and the only one in the entry** — „а када му беше три године, она га научи вери и молитви“, and when he was three years old she taught him the faith and prayer as much as a child of that age could receive — and nothing is reckoned from 304 by it, though 301 would be the answer and would be a birth year invented out of a mother’s catechesis. `types` UNTOUCHED at `martyr`, which „муч.“ is. **`virgin` and `infant` are not on offer**, the second not being a word this vocabulary has at all. No `office`, no `locations` — Iconium, Lycaonia, Seleucia and Ohrid are a narrative. **NO NEW `related` ROWS.** The mother is already two-way. The judge who took the child on his knees and then dashed him to the ground is unnamed, Diocletian is an emperor, and the church of the Holy Theotokos Bolnička at Ohrid, where the book says a part of their relics lies, is **a church and not a folder** — a dedication is not a relation, which is the rule §6 states and which this day could have broken twice. **WHAT IS NEW IS THE CHILD’S OWN WORDS AND HIS OWN ACT.** The judge, to grieve her and shake her, took the child in his arms and began to caress him; and Cyricus cried out at the top of his voice „Ја сам хришћанин, пусти ме матери!“ — I am a Christian, let me go to my mother — **and began to scratch the judge with his little hands, turning his face away from him**; at which the judge grew angry, struck the child against the ground and pushed him away with his foot, and the child rolled down the stone steps and gave up his holy and innocent soul to God. **And his mother’s response is the entry’s point**: seeing how Cyricus suffered before her, Julitta was joyful and gave thanks to God that He had counted her son worthy of a martyr’s crown. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Chiric și Iulita, mama lui», Glasul 4 — the common of martyrs, printed there under the two names; the spelling «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own.

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contest won from You, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Your strength they overthrew their tormentors and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. At their prayers, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ἡ καλλιμάρτυς τοῦ Χρίστου Ἰουλίττα, σὺν τριετεῖ ἀμνῶ αὐτῆς τῷ Κηρύκῳ, δικαστοὺ πρὸ βήματος παρέστησαν φαιδρῶς, εὔτολμοι κηρύττοντες. τὴν χριστώνυμον κλῆσιν, ἄμφω μὴ πτοούμενοι, ἀπειλᾶς τῶν τυρράνων καὶ στεφηφόροι νῦν ἐν οὐρανοίς, ἀγαλλιώνται. Χριστῷ παριστάμενοι.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ', Ὁ ὑψωθεῖς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ — the only hymn on the page of «Άγιοι Κήρυκος και Ιουλίττα η μητέρα του», and it names both of them

english.text: Julitta, the fair martyr of Christ, together with Cyricus her three-year-old lamb, stood brightly before the judge's seat, preaching with courage the name of Christians; neither of them was dismayed at the threats of the tyrants, and now, crowned, they rejoice in the heavens, standing before Christ.
